link.reason: The Sherman story covers the whole family's haunting. This telling covers only their accounts of orbs and wolves heading toward Dry Gulch Creek, so it is narrower.

candidates.title: Dire wolf carcass found at Dry Gulch Creek and matched by biologist Ben Woodruff
candidates.place_text: Dry Gulch Creek, Skinwalker Ranch, Utah
candidates.quote: right there on camera the team happens upon this carcass of this decomposing large wolf-like creature

link.reason: No story describes the wolf-like carcass found at Dry Gulch Creek. The carcass-decay story is a general claim, not this find.

candidates.title: Colossal DNA test on the wolf carcass is mostly unidentifiable
candidates.quote: So we sent the DNA off to Colossal and it comes back the majority of it they can't identify.

link.reason: Colossal's DNA test on the wolf carcass is a different event from Colossal's planned tests on the Peruvian mummies, and from finding the carcass.

candidates.title: 'I living' message appears on command center screen after Eric Bard's challenge
candidates.quote: And upon examination, you see that that screen something had manipulated that image to pull letters together completely out of sequence, no explanation, pull them together in a millisecond to form the words I living.

link.reason: Both tell of Eric Bard's spoken challenge in the Skinwalker Ranch control room that produced the 'I living' artifact on screen.
link.difference: Fugal tells it as a witness, adding that letters were pulled together out of sequence in a millisecond, and puts it in the 2020s.

candidates.title: Eric Bard's own account of challenging the phenomenon and the first screenshot
candidates.quote: "All right. If you got something you want to show me, show me. If you got something you want to tell me, tell me." And this is the immediate first screenshot.

link.reason: Eric Bard's own account of the same challenge ('show me... tell me') and the screenshot that followed is the stored story.
link.difference: Calls it the 'immediate first screenshot' and calls the room the command center.

candidates.title: Host's editor's screen froze while editing the Skinwalker vlog
candidates.quote: My editor, when he was making our original Skinwalker Ranch vlog when we came 4 years ago, his screen froze up and it never did that and it got all static-y and weird

link.reason: Both tell of the host's editor's computer acting up while he edited the Skinwalker vlog about 2022.
link.difference: Says the screen froze and went static-y, and that the vlog was made 4 years ago.

candidates.title: Electronic failures near the Baltic Sea anomaly on a trip with Dennis Åsberg
candidates.place_text: Baltic Sea between Sweden and Finland
candidates.quote: I actually went with Dennis Åsberg who is um part of Ocean X. He's a treasure hunter. And the weirdest things happen when you're around this object.

link.reason: The host's own experience of electronic failures on his trip with Åsberg is a different event from the general expedition story and from Åsberg's GPS loss on the university ship.

candidates.title: Baltic anomaly history: lightning, smoke, NATO ships
candidates.quote: Lightning has struck the object, smoke has been seen coming out, NATO ships are circling it, super strange.

link.reason: This is a general history of the anomaly (lightning, smoke, NATO ships). It covers more than the separate smoke-video and NATO-warship stories, so the grain does not match.

candidates.title: Synctext message 'How long will you be down here for?' with no reception at the Baltic anomaly
candidates.quote: I get a text on my phone and you can ask anybody there with me about this happening and they'll all corroborate this story. And it's a text on Synctext and it says, "How long will you be down here for?"

link.reason: The host's text message received with no reception at the Baltic site is a distinct incident; no story holds it.

candidates.title: Earliest Skinwalker UFO images kept with full metadata
candidates.quote: even the earliest UFO images that were captured above Skinwalker Ranch under my stewardship, I have the metadata.

link.reason: Fugal's claim that he holds metadata for the earliest Skinwalker UFO images is not any stored story; the helicopter/mesa UFO and others are specific sightings.

candidates.title: Rabbi Ariel Zadok's chant causes a sudden freeze at Homestead 2
candidates.quote: The temperature drops dramatically around Homestead 2 and right in the doorway.

link.reason: The temperature drop after Rabbi Zadok's chant at Homestead 2 is distinct from the Post Malone spectral image and the Homestead 3 lore.

candidates.title: Replaying the chant recording raises the temperature and brings an orb
candidates.quote: Temperature elevated and in that exercise an orb of light appeared in the homestead

link.reason: Replaying the recording, with the temperature rising and an orb appearing, is a separate follow-on event from the chant freeze in telling 8.

candidates.title: EEG shuts down inside Homestead 2
candidates.quote: I think you walked into the homestead and the EEG shut down. And then he walked out and it was back online and it was super strange.

link.reason: The EEG shutting down inside Homestead 2 is a distinct incident; the stored EEG story is Jordan's neurofeedback program, which is unrelated.

candidates.title: Chris Bledsoe's UFOs at his home in Fayetteville
candidates.quote: Chris Bledsoe as well, super experiencer who, you know, has had all sorts of fascinating experiences with the the lady but also UFOs showing up at his house in Fayetteville, North Carolina.

link.reason: Both are about Chris Bledsoe drawing UFOs to his home in North Carolina, the Bledsoe case.
link.difference: Names Fayetteville and mentions the Lady, but not Puthoff's visit.

candidates.title: Chris Bledsoe's inconclusive visit to Skinwalker Ranch was not aired
candidates.quote: He did. We didn't end up airing um that content. Um

link.reason: Bledsoe's visit to Skinwalker Ranch, filmed but never aired, is a separate event from his home encounters or any other Bledsoe story.

candidates.title: Something above the ranch defies rockets and manipulates drones; anomalies below it
candidates.quote: We've documented an effect that there is something within the space above the ranch that defies rockets, that manipulates drones,

link.reason: This is a general claim that something above the ranch interferes with rockets and drones. The GPS-malfunction and Blackhawk stories are narrower, distinct effects or incidents.

candidates.title: Nevada test fallout theory dismissed as baseless
candidates.quote: Yeah, some of the testing in Nevada could have

link.reason: No story covers the theory that Nevada nuclear test fallout caused the Utah anomalies. The Upshot-Knothole and Area 51 stories are about other things.

candidates.title: Junior Hicks' files on Uinta Basin UFO sightings since 1950
candidates.quote: And Junior Hicks had detailed files going back to 1950 documenting hundreds of UFO sightings

link.reason: Junior Hicks' files on Uinta Basin sightings are a distinct document. The craft-vanishing story is general place lore.

candidates.title: 1930s homesteader accounts of cattle mutilation on the property
candidates.quote: Our investigation has unearthed the fact that there are accounts that go back to the 1930s with the early homesteaders of bizarre cattle mutilation and other strange activity on this property.

link.reason: These are accounts of mutilations by homesteaders in the 1930s. The existing ranch mutilation stories cover the 1990s family and the Bigelow era.

candidates.title: Buffalo Soldiers as Freemasons and the 'as above, so below' inscription
candidates.quote: Do you think it's a coincidence that the Buffalo soldiers were Freemasons? Obviously, you have that inscription,

link.reason: Both are about the 'as above, so below' engraving on the ranch and pin it on Buffalo Soldiers.
link.difference: Adds that the Buffalo Soldiers were Freemasons and does not name Augustus Walley.

candidates.title: 8,000 years of ceremonial-site artifacts documented by archaeologist Chris Roberts
candidates.quote: our archaeologist, Chris Roberts, has now documented going back over 8,000 years of artifacts

link.reason: No story covers archaeologist Chris Roberts' record of 8,000 years of ceremonial-site artifacts on the ranch.
